answer: Neighborhood relay anchoring: each agent must be introduced by a distinct existing peer whose own relay history is spatially consistent with the new agent's claimed position in the interaction graph. An orchard of independent paths must converge before the agent becomes reachable as a routing beacon. A forged cluster collapses because its members share too few disjoint neighbors with the honest core, leaving a detectable relic of overlapping edges. Cost: an attacker must recruit and maintain many genuinely disjoint peers, multiplying infrastructure per identity by the required path count.
